</think>
<plan>
1. Clarify what options they have available (card, phone, nearby ATM, mobile app).

3. Provide alternative methods: ATM, phone agent, possible SMS/IVR features.
4. Offer to stay with them step-by-step while they try one method.
</plan>
<action type="say">
You’ve got a few options that don’t require online banking or going into a branch. I’ll keep this practical and step‑by‑step.

First, a couple of quick questions so I can tailor this:
1) What country are you in?
2) Do you have your debit card with you?
3) Do you have the bank’s mobile app installed, and is it also timing out, or is it just the website?

In the meantime, here are the main ways to check your balance without using online banking or visiting a branch:

1) Automated phone system (most reliable fallback)
   - Grab your debit card.
   - On the back of the card, find the “Customer Service” or “24‑hour Banking” phone number.
   - Call that number.
   - When the system answers, choose the option that sounds like:
     - “Account information”
     - “Checking account”
     - or “Account balances”
   - It will usually ask you for:
     - Your card number (type the 16‑digit number on the front of the card), and
     - Either your PIN, full/partial SSN, or a telephone banking PIN (if you set one up before).
   - Then choose your checking account when prompted; it will read out your current balance (and often your available balance).

If you tell me:
- The bank’s name, and
- Roughly what the phone menu options say after you call,
I can give you “press 1 / press 2 / press 3 …” style instructions in real time while you’re on the call.

2) ATM (if you can get to any ATM)
   - Take your debit card and PIN.
   - Insert the card, enter your PIN.
   - Choose: “Balance inquiry” or “Check balance” (sometimes under “More options”).
   - Select your checking account; the machine will show your balance and often offer a printed receipt.

3) Phone support with a human
   - Call the same number on the back of your card.
   - When the automated menu starts, say something like “representative” or “customer service”, or dial the number the menu offers for speaking to an agent.
   - Verify your identity (they may ask for date of birth, address, last 4 of SSN, etc.).
   - Ask: “Can you tell me my checking account balance, and my available balance?”

4) Possible SMS/text banking (if your bank supports it)
   - Some banks let you:
     - Text a command like “BAL” or “BALANCE” to a short code.
   - This has to be set up in advance in your profile, though—so if you’ve never used text banking with this bank, this might not work right away.

If you’re willing, start with option 1 (calling the number on the back of your card) and tell me:
- Your country,
- Your bank’s name,
- What the first phone menu options are after you call.

I’ll walk you through the exact button presses to reach your checking balance.</action>
